title: Defined Media Primary Mouse Hippocampal Neuron Culture
author: Kristopher Plambeck
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bb47iqzn
materials: Replace media with NBC. Media Formulations: Dissection Buffer
·5 mL Sodium Pyruvate Neuronal Plating Media (NPM)
mL B-27 after filter sterilizing Additional Solutions: Poly-L-Lysine Solution (PLL): PLL stocks are at 200 mg/mL located in the -20C fridge. For 25 ug/mL:
·Bring up to 1 L with milli-Q water

steps.title: Prepare wax‑coated coverslips
steps.instruction: Wash each coverslip three times with distilled water, melt wax pellets, and apply wax dots to the four corners of each coverslip before drying.

substeps.instruction: Wash coverslips 3× with distilled water.
Melt wax pellets: place wax pellets in a small beaker, set the beaker in a second beaker of boiling water on a hot plate.
Using a 200 µL pipette, carefully add a wax dot to each corner of every coverslip.
Transfer the wax‑dot‑treated coverslips to 6‑well plates (minimum four plates, 24 coverslips total) inside a biosafety cabinet.
Place the plates back in the biosafety cabinet to allow the wax dots to dry.

steps.title: Sterilize work area
steps.instruction: Create a sterile bench environment before handling the coverslips.

substeps.instruction: Turn on a Bunsen burner and place it near the hot plate.
Wipe the bench surface with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Genotype pups
steps.instruction: Identify wild‑type and knockout pups by tail‑snip DNA extraction and PCR.

substeps.instruction: Use a Sharpie to number each pup on the belly.
Snip a small piece of tail from each pup and place it in an individually numbered tube.
Digest the tail snips and perform DNA extraction and genotyping according to the Diaz Lab genotyping protocol.
Separate wild‑type from knockout animals and keep only the selected genotype for dissection.

steps.title: Prepare media and reagents
steps.instruction: Make all solutions required for dissection, plating, and culture.

substeps.instruction: Dissection Buffer: add 7.5 mL of 30 % glucose stock to DI water to obtain a final 0.45 % glucose solution.

Neurobasal complete (NBC) 500 mL: combine Neurobasal (473 mL, i.e., remove 27 mL from a 500 mL stock), 5 mL HEPES, 5 mL sodium pyruvate, 5 mL penicillin/streptomycin, and 1.5 mL L‑glutamine. Filter‑sterilize the final solution.

Poly‑L‑lysine (PLL) solutions: dilute stock at 1:8,000 in 0.1 M borate buffer (add 6.25 µL PLL to 50 mL 0.1 M borate) for a 1 mg/mL working solution; alternatively dilute at 1:200 (add 50 µL PLL to 10 mL 0.1 M borate) for higher concentration.
Add the appropriate volume of 70 % w/w 15.8 N nitric acid to 250 mL water as indicated in the original protocol (exact volume not specified).
Place dissection tools in a dry heat oven at 250 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Dissect hippocampi and enzymatic digestion
steps.instruction: Isolate hippocampi from P0‑P2 pups and digest them to obtain a single‑cell suspension.

substeps.instruction: Decapitate each pup and remove the brain; place brains in ice‑cold dissection buffer.
Under a dissecting microscope, isolate the hippocampi, carefully removing meninges, and transfer them to a 15 mL conical tube on ice.
Transfer hippocampi to a new 15 mL tube containing 5 mL HBSS plus 100 µL 2.5 % trypsin (Gibco).
Add the unspecified volume of papain (Worthington) to the same 5 mL HBSS, warm the mixture in a 37 °C water bath to aid dissolution, and filter‑sterilize before use.
Incubate the hippocampi in the 37 °C water bath for 12–15 minutes, inverting gently every few minutes.

steps.title: Terminate digestion and collect cells
steps.instruction: Stop enzymatic activity, centrifuge, and begin mechanical dissociation.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL Neurobasal plating medium (NPM) to the tube after incubation.
Centrifuge the suspension for 5 minutes at 1000 rpm.
Carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 3 mL NPM.
Pipette the suspension up and down with a 1 mL pipette 3–5 times, then triturate with a fire‑polished long‑stem pipette (no more than 12 strokes).
If tissue chunks remain, allow them to settle and remove the chunks.

steps.title: Adjust final volume and count cells
steps.instruction: Bring the cell suspension to a known volume and determine viable cell density.

substeps.instruction: Add NPM to bring the total volume to 5–10 mL as needed.
Mix 45 µL of cell suspension with 5 µL trypan blue and count viable cells using a hemocytometer (dead cells appear blue; exclude them).
Viability should be ≥80 % at this stage.

steps.title: Plate neurons on coverslips
steps.instruction: Dilute cells to the desired density and seed onto poly‑L‑lysine‑coated coverslips.

substeps.instruction: Dilute the cell suspension to 25,000 cells/mL (or 75,000 cells/mL depending on desired final density) with NPM, accounting for pipetting error.
Add 2 mL of the diluted suspension to each well containing a poly‑L‑lysine‑coated coverslip; this yields a final density of 50,000 cells per well (or 150,000 cells per well as indicated).
Place the plates in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for 5–6 hours.

steps.title: Initial media replacement
steps.instruction: Replace the plating medium with Neurobasal complete (NBC) after the initial attachment period.

substeps.instruction: After 5–6 hours, carefully remove the plating medium and add fresh NBC to each well.

steps.title: AraC treatment and routine media changes
steps.instruction: Add antimitotic agent AraC on specified days and perform regular media refreshes.

substeps.instruction: Day 6 (4 DIV): add AraC from a 10 mM stock to achieve a final concentration of 5 µM in each well (add 2.5 µL AraC to 5 mL NBC; 1:2000 dilution).
Repeat the same AraC addition on Days 7 (5 DIV), 12 (10 DIV), 17 (15 DIV), and 21 (20 DIV).
At each media‑change time point, remove ___ µL of spent media and replace with 1 mL fresh NBC.
